source: Bombardier Global 7500 brochure (2018), p. 35, the starboard render, at 300 dpi (3450 x 2400 px). Hand-digitised and the camera solved by the water engineer's session ('Water realism and appearance'), 2026-09-23, handed over for phase 3c, part 6 (docs/findings/GLOBAL_LIVERY.md).

camera.about: A pinhole solved on the render's 15 cabin windows (centre, top and bottom; rms 0.84 px), the cabin's top rim (614 columns, rms 0.41 px) and the forward belly edge (157 columns, rms 0.47 px): 49.7 degrees forward of abeam, 6.0 above, 242 m out. Body metres (x forward, y up, z starboard) to camera: pc = R (p - centre), R from the rotation vector (axis times angle, radians); u = principal.u + focal pc.x / pc.z, v = principal.v + focal pc.y / pc.z, v down. The station anchor is p. 29's: the front window 6.40 m aft of the tip.

noseEdge.about: The nose's upper outline, digitised by hand column by column: the first row of aircraft under the background (clouds and sky), sub-pixel. 'glass' where the windshield itself forms the outline. A 1-4 px darker rim hugs the edge outside these points; if it is skin, every residual shrinks by up to 0.04 m.
